task.description: Idiom/scope/decision-record-consistency gate on ISS-0692's design amendment, run after SECURITY-REVIEWER's PASS.
acceptance_criteria: New §1.5 checked for stylistic/structural consistency with §1.3/§1.4
Scope-creep check across all commits since 35d3489a
visual-baseline.ts JSDoc addition checked for idiom and inertness
Independent judgment on whether a regression test is warranted for Step 4

result.summary:
Checked out feature/WF03-ISS0692-20260917 (already at HEAD aaf60c24, fetch/pull --ff-only confirmed up to date). Read ISS-0692.yaml, the full req362-visual-regression-testing.md design doc (not just §1.5), step-02/step-02b (v1 FAIL + v2 PASS)/step-03c handoffs, and `git diff 35d3489a..HEAD` plus `git log 35d3489a..HEAD --oneline` (6 commits, all ISS-0692-scoped).

1. STYLE/STRUCTURE CONSISTENCY (§1.5 vs §1.3/§1.4): §1.5 uses '###'-level heading numbering identical to its siblings, and internally uses bold lead-in pseudo-headers ('**Decision, stated as an invariant...**', '**Existing baseline checked...**', '**Why this needs to be said here...**', '**Enforcement note...**') rather than §1.3/§1.4's plainer bullet-paragraph style. This is not a foreign pattern introduced by this change: §3.3 and §3.4 elsewhere in the same document already use bold-prefixed lead sentences in lieu of sub-headings ('**This design does not loosen...**', '**Explicit statement, as AC-6 requires:**', '**Why, stated so a future reader does not soften this:**'). §1.5 is consistent with the document's own established variety of internal structure, not an outlier. AC map row format in §7 matches the table's existing row shape exactly. No finding.

2. SCOPE CREEP: `git log 35d3489a..HEAD --oneline` shows 6 commits, all narrowly ISS-0692-scoped: (09617d87) the original §1.5 amendment, (c104ccbc/281bd0c2) handoff bookkeeping, (6f9f6891) CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR FAIL record, (ca4e4924) the one-paragraph factual correction, (aaf60c24) CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR PASS record. `git diff 35d3489a..HEAD --stat` touches exactly 4 files: two handoff JSONs, the design doc (+84/-0), and visual-baseline.ts (+10/-0). No application code, no migration, no unrelated doc edited. Matches ISS-0692's affected_files list exactly. No finding.

3. DECISION-RECORD CONSISTENCY: Searched docs/migration/decisions/ for PII/redaction/synthetic/sensitive/fixture-data policy. Found only application-level redaction records unrelated to UAT test-fixture policy: 0019 (query-DSL field-grant redaction), 0022/0023/0030 (Letflow.Entities.Query.FieldGrants -- field-level redaction of exam candidate answers from other candidates, a runtime authorization mechanism). None of these govern UAT scenario/baseline fixture data content, and §1.5 does not conflict with or silently re-decide any of them -- they solve a different problem (hiding real production-adjacent fields from an under-privileged runtime viewer) from what §1.5 solves (keeping test fixture content itself synthetic so a permanently-committed test artifact never carries real PII in the first place). §1.5 correctly distinguishes itself from a FieldGrants-style redaction approach in its own rejection reasoning (redaction of a screenshot is rejected for a different, sound reason -- incompatibility with §3.4's unconditional pixel-diff -- not because FieldGrants exists). No decision record addresses UAT/visual-baseline fixture-data policy today, so there is nothing for this amendment to contradict; recording the policy directly in the design doc (rather than spinning up a new docs/migration/decisions/ record) is one of the two remediation paths ISS-0692's own FIX DIRECTION explicitly offered ('extend the design (or add a follow-up decision record)'), so this is not a case of silently bypassing the decision-record process -- it's the option the issue itself sanctioned. No finding.

4. VISUAL-BASELINE.TS JSDOC ADDITION: Re-read the diff directly. Two JSDoc block-comment insertions, one above `acceptBaseline` and one above `rebaseline`, each following the file's existing JSDoc convention of citing the design section it implements (the pre-existing comments already say things like 'design §2.2 step 4' and 'design §4.3' -- the new paragraphs follow the identical citation style, 'Data-sensitivity precondition (design §1.5): ...'). Confirmed independently (not just trusting SECURITY-REVIEWER's or CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR's prior confirmation) that no non-comment line is touched in either hunk -- both insertions land strictly between existing `/**`...`*/` boundaries and the function signatures/bodies below them are byte-identical to the pre-image. Genuinely inert. No finding.

5. HANDOFF/REWORK HYGIENE: step-02b's v1 result is preserved as `result_v1_superseded` (not deleted or silently overwritten) alongside the v2 `result_v2` that superseded it, with an explicit `status_history_note` explaining which is authoritative -- this matches core-directives.md's discipline against silently rewriting a record's factual history (the same discipline flagged in docs/anti-patterns.md's handoff-integrity entries). step-02-code-designer.json's original (factually wrong) `result.summary` was likewise left untouched, with the correction carried in a separate `rework_note` field that explicitly disclaims the superseded paragraph rather than editing it in place. `rework_count`/`max_rework` fields are present and consistent (1 of 3) on both files that went through a FAIL cycle. next_action chains correctly at each step (CODE-DESIGNER -> CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR -> SECURITY-REVIEWER -> REVIEWER). No finding.

6. REGRESSION-TEST APPLICABILITY (independent judgment, not deferred to Step 4): I agree no regression test is warranted. The entire change set is (a) a design-doc amendment with zero executable content, and (b) two JSDoc comment blocks in visual-baseline.ts independently re-confirmed (twice now, by SECURITY-REVIEWER and again here) to touch no executable line -- `acceptBaseline`/`rebaseline`'s signatures, bodies, and error-throwing behavior are byte-for-byte unchanged from before ISS-0692. There is no behavior change to regress-test. A test would only make sense if this fix had chosen a mechanical enforcement path (a redaction transform or a synthetic-data validator) -- it explicitly did not, per §1.5's own 'no code change is required' framing, which this review confirms is an accurate characterization of what was actually built, not a hand-wave around missing test coverage.

No type-safety gap, no OTP/supervision concern applies -- this change touches no gen_statem, no supervisor, no runtime process boundary.

Overall: idiomatic for a design-doc amendment, correctly scoped, does not contradict any existing decision record (none exists on this specific topic, and the issue itself authorized a design-doc-level fix as an alternative to a new decision record), the code-adjacent comment change is genuinely inert and stylistically consistent, and handoff/rework bookkeeping through the FAIL->rework->PASS cycle followed the project's non-destructive-correction convention correctly.
